headline: Today's 12 km at a brisker pace sat mid-range on HR, following yesterday's long run — solid back-to-back durability.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
You've effectively strung together a longer easy run and a quicker, moderate-effort session on consecutive days — the first genuine back-to-back pairing to appear recently, which is exactly the durability quality that matters most a month out from a self-supported multi-day crossing. Today ran nearly a full minute per km quicker than yesterday's 21 km, yet the heart rate stayed comfortably below your threshold, so this reads as controlled aerobic work rather than a hard session stacked onto fatigue.

The medium-term picture stays intact: volume has stepped up meaningfully over the prior block, strength frequency has more than doubled, and your comparable-effort easy-run HR continues to run lower than the previous period. That combination — more load, more strength, lower cost per easy effort — is consistent with genuine aerobic consolidation rather than accumulating strain, and the strain:tolerance ratio sitting in a maintaining band supports that.

One thing the recent weeks still haven't rehearsed for St. Olavsleden specifically: pack-loaded running and sustained climbing. Yesterday's elevation was the best of the block, but the terrain you're heading into asks for more of both. Worth noting, not correcting mid-week.
watch_items: Whether pack-loaded running finally enters the week, since the self-supported crossing is now close.
Whether per-run elevation keeps building toward the sustained border-section climb.
Whether short-sleep nights like the most recent one cluster or stay isolated as longer sessions re-enter the schedule.
Whether this back-to-back pairing repeats, confirming durability rather than a one-off.
